title: Oxycodone-naloxone in Relieving Opioid-related Constipation
brief_summary: The primary objective of this study is to demonstrate that subjects with moderate to severe non-malignant pain taking oxycodone/naloxone prolonged release tablets have improvement in symptoms of constipation compared to subjects taking oxycodone prolonged release tablets alone.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Male or female subjects at lest 18 years or older with pain.
* Subjects must report constipation caused or aggravated by opioids.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Females who are pregnant or lactating.
* Subjects with evidence of significant structural abnormalities of the gastrointestinal (GI) tract (e.g. bowel obstruction, strictures).
